questions.question_text: A 58-year-old man drinks eight units of alcohol after work each night. He becomes violent when drinking and is hospitalized after an alcohol-related brawl. He tells the psychiatrist that he has been drinking for many years and is not willing to cut down on his alcohol intake. He also rejects a hotline number to an additional treatment facility nearby. According to the stages of change, which stage is he in?
questions.explanation:
In this example, the man’s level of motivation is consistent with the precontemplation stage, as he has little or no motivation to change his behaviour. Prochaska and DiClemente’s stages of change applied to alcohol abuse or dependence describe an individual’s level of motivation for recovery. The model consists of five stages of change:
1. Precontemplation, where there is no interest in change in the foreseeable future (next 6 months).
2. Contemplation, where the individual considers change in the next 1–6 months but not immediately.
3. Preparation, which involves planning on change in the next month.
4. Action, where meaningful changes were made in the recent past (6 months).
5. Maintenance, which refers to maintaining change for 6 months or more.

questions.question_text: A 20-year-old pregnant woman is heroin dependent. She insists on undergoing heroin withdrawal and asks you for advice. In this case, in which period would withdrawal cause least harm to the baby?
questions.explanation: If a pregnant woman decides to withdraw from heroin, it should be done during the second trimester, as it then poses the least harm to the baby and has the lowest association with miscarriage. Withdrawal during the first trimester may cause spontaneous abortion and during the third trimester poses a risk of delivering premature babies, which have a poorer chance of survival and greater incidence of permanent disability. The patient should be put on methadone maintenance treatment after withdrawal. Methadone maintenance improves birth weight but may depress respiration in the newborn and may lead to a more severe and prolonged withdrawal syndrome, with higher frequencies of seizures. Newborn infants should be kept in hospital for at least 2 weeks. Respiratory depression may be treated with naloxone and seizures and withdrawal by sedatives such as diazepam.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding the correlation coefficient is false?

options.text: A correlation coefficient can be strong but statistically non-significant because of the sample size.
Correlation describes the strength of the linear relationship between variables, which is denoted by the correlation coefficient (r).
Spearman’s and Kendall’s rank coefficients are the non-parametric alternatives to Pearson’s correlation coefficient.
The value of the correlation coefficient can range from −2 to +2.
A value of 0.2–0.5 signifies moderate correlation.

correct_answer.text: The value of the correlation coefficient can range from −2 to +2.

correct_answers.text: The value of the correlation coefficient can range from −2 to +2.

questions.explanation: The correlation coefficient is an index that quantifies the linear relationship between a pair of variables. Various correlation coefficients are available, all taking values between −1 and 1, with the extreme values indicating a perfect linear relationship and the sign indicating the direction of the relationship. A value of 0 indicates that there is no linear relationship between the two variables, although there may be a more esoteric nonlinear relationship. The most common of such coefficient is Pearson’s product moment correlation coefficient, which acts as an estimator of the population correlation in a bivariate normal distribution. The degree of correlation is represented by the r-value. r-value (degree of correlation): 0–0.2 (negligible), 0.2–0.5 (weak), 0.5–0.8 (moderate) and 0.8–1.0 (strong).

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding standard deviation (SD) is true?

options.text: For a sample size of 20, a good estimate of population SD can be obtained by using 20 in the denominator of the equation.
SD has the same units as the original observation.
SD is more difficult to calculate than quartile distribution.
Variance is the square root of the SD.

correct_answer.text: SD has the same units as the original observation.

correct_answers.text: SD has the same units as the original observation.

questions.explanation: SD is the most commonly used measure of the spread of a set of observations. It is equal to the square root of the variance. A low SD indicates that the data points tend to be very close to the mean (also called expected value); a high SD indicates that the data points are spread out over a large range of values. A useful property of SD is that, unlike the variance, it is expressed in the same units as the data. For a sample size of 20, the denominator should be 19, degree of freedom = n – 1. SD is always positive.

questions.question_text: A 52-year-old man drinks eight bottles of beer every other night. He reports feeling jittery if he does not drink, and he uses shots of alcohol to get him through the day. He is seeing a psychologist, who uses a technique that is described using the acronym FRAMES. Which of the following is not part of the acronym FRAMES?
questions.explanation:
The acronym ‘FRAMES’ stands for
• Personalized feedback or assessment results detailing the target behaviour and associated effects and consequences on the individual
• Emphasizing the individual’s responsibility for change
• Giving advice on how to change
• Providing a menu of options for change
• Expressing empathy through behaviours conveying caring, understanding and warmth
• Emphasizing self-efficacy for change and instilling hope that change is not only possible but also within reach

questions.question_text: A 37-year-old woman lies in bed all day. She cries herself to sleep every night and has lost 18 kg over the past 2 years. She has attempted suicide several times and is currently hospitalized for her most recent attempt. Which of the following treatment options is contraindicated in the initial stage of her condition?
questions.explanation: Specific contraindications for brief psychodynamic therapy are severe depression, acute psychosis and borderline personality disorder. General contraindications are when the therapist is unable to make effective contact with the patient and when there is evidence of a need for extended work with the patient.

questions.question_text: Based on the latest evidence on the treatment for mild cognitive impairment, which of the following demonstrates the strongest evidence?

options.text: Cholinesterase inhibitors do not reduce the frequency of incident dementia.
Huannao Yicong improves cognition and social functioning.

correct_answer.text: Cholinesterase inhibitors do not reduce the frequency of incident dementia.

correct_answers.text: Cholinesterase inhibitors do not reduce the frequency of incident dementia.

questions.explanation: A systematic review found that cholinesterase inhibitors did not reduce the frequency of mild cognitive impairment leading to dementia. Single trials showed modest benefits for other interventions but not for incident dementia prevention.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the least common feature of Cushing’s syndrome of endogenous origin?
questions.explanation: Mania is less common than depression in endogenous Cushing’s syndrome; depression, cognitive impairment and guilt delusions are frequent, and second-person hallucinations can occur.

questions.question_text: The percentage of patients with delirium who have abnormal tracing detected on their EEG is
questions.explanation: Approximately 90% of patients with delirium have abnormal EEG tracings, such as delta activity, asymmetry or diffuse slowing.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the neurobiology of ageing is incorrect?

options.text: In normal ageing, there is a slow reduction in the weight and the volume of the human brain with an increase in the size of the ventricles after the age of 50 years.
All neuroanatomical areas in the brain show significant loss of neurons with normal ageing.
The absolute rate of nerve cells loss is around 1% per year after the age of 60 years.
Lipofuscin accumulates in the cytoplasm of the nerve cells from childhood.
Tau protein is involved in the linking of neurofilaments and microtubules and accumulates in a small proportion of ageing nerve cells.

correct_answer.text: All neuroanatomical areas in the brain show significant loss of neurons with normal ageing.

correct_answers.text: All neuroanatomical areas in the brain show significant loss of neurons with normal ageing.

questions.explanation: Not all brain areas lose neurons with normal ageing. Loss is regionally selective, affecting frontal cortex, hippocampus, locus coeruleus and substantia nigra more than other areas.

questions.question_text: What is the approximate incidence of delirium amongst old people who are hospitalized?
questions.explanation: Delirium occurs in about 5–10% of older hospitalized patients, with higher rates in specific subgroups (e.g. hip fracture, intensive care).

questions.question_text: Based on the 10th Revision of International Classification of Disease (ICD-10) criteria, which of the following statements regarding moderate mental retardation is false?

options.text: The intelligence quotient (IQ) score range is usually below that of 49.
It is often associated with epilepsy and neurological and other disabilities.
At least 20% of neurofibromatosis type I (NF-1) sufferers present with moderate-to-severe learning disability (LD).

correct_answer.text: At least 20% of neurofibromatosis type I (NF-1) sufferers present with moderate-to-severe learning disability (LD).

correct_answers.text: At least 20% of neurofibromatosis type I (NF-1) sufferers present with moderate-to-severe learning disability (LD).

questions.explanation: More than 50% of individuals with NF-1 have learning disabilities, many of which are moderate to severe—not only 20%.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a characteristic of children with Prader–Willi syndrome?
questions.explanation: Prader–Willi syndrome features hypotonia in infancy (not spasticity), hyperphagia leading to obesity, characteristic facial features and hypogonadism.

questions.question_text: Which of the following syndromes does not present with microcephaly?
questions.explanation: Neurofibromatosis typically presents with macrocephaly rather than microcephaly; the other listed syndromes often feature small head size.

questions.question_text: Which of the following conditions is most frequently seen with autism?
questions.explanation: Attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder (hyperkinetic disorder) co-occurs in up to 50% of children with autism.

questions.question_text: An 18-year-old lady complains of low mood, irritability and insomnia prior to her menses. Which of the following medications would you recommend?
questions.explanation: SSRIs such as sertraline are effective for premenstrual dysphoric symptoms, improving both psychological and physical premenstrual complaints.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding depression in multiple sclerosis (MS) is false?

options.text: Major depressive disorder (MDD) occurs more when MS involves the cerebellum rather than the spinal cord.
MDD occurs in up to 50% of patients during their lifetime.
Selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) should be used with caution, as it may increase spasticity.
Rates of depression in first-degree relatives of depressed patients with MS are higher than the rates of depression in first-degree relatives of people who do not have MS.
MS-induced cognitive impairment is not a risk factor for suicide.

correct_answer.text: Rates of depression in first-degree relatives of depressed patients with MS are higher than the rates of depression in first-degree relatives of people who do not have MS.

correct_answers.text: Rates of depression in first-degree relatives of depressed patients with MS are higher than the rates of depression in first-degree relatives of people who do not have MS.

questions.explanation: Genetic linkage for MS is limited; first-degree relatives of depressed MS patients have a LOWER rate of depression than relatives of non-MS depressed patients.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about the treatment of depression in patients with Parkinson disorder is incorrect?

options.text: Remeron should not be considered, as it may worsen sleep quality.
It is important to optimize treatment of motor symptoms.
SSRI has been considered to be the first-line treatment for depression.
Bupropion is contraindicated due to its side effect profile.

correct_answer.text: Bupropion is contraindicated due to its side effect profile.

correct_answers.text: Bupropion is contraindicated due to its side effect profile.

questions.explanation: Bupropion is not contraindicated and may be beneficial for Parkinson’s-related depression. SSRIs remain first-line, optimizing motor therapy is essential, and tricyclics are preferably avoided.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most likely to be associated with juvenile delinquency?

options.text: Oppositional defiant disorder in parents when they were younger

questions.explanation: Juvenile delinquency has been linked to parental criminality, conduct disorder in childhood, low IQ and unsatisfactory child-rearing practices.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the best predictor of future violent behaviour?
questions.explanation: The single best predictor of future violence is a history of past violence.

questions.question_text: The most common precipitating factor leading to deliberate self-poisoning and self-injury in children and adolescents under 16 years of age is related to which of the following?
questions.explanation: Studies show the most frequent precipitant in under-16s is relationship difficulties with parents, followed by issues with friends.

questions.question_text: A recent study has found that a single-nucleotide polymorphism (SNP) of the dopamine receptor-3 (DRD3) gene (rs167771) is associated with autism. Which of the following neuroanatomical areas is associated with the alleles of the rs167771 SNP and explains symptoms of autism?
questions.explanation: Variants of the DRD3 rs167771 SNP correlate with altered striatal volumes, which link to stereotyped behaviors seen in autism.

questions.question_text: Which of the following modalities of treatment has been shown to be most effective for children with conduct disorder?
questions.explanation: Multimodal approaches combining parent management training, individual therapy and family interventions yield the best outcomes in childhood conduct disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements about obsessive-compulsive disorder (OCD) is incorrect?

options.text: OCD affects an approximate 3% of adults and children.
Relief of anxiety reduction is an important maintaining factor of the obsessive-compulsive symptoms.
The association between OCD and suicidality is weak.
Most patients respond to serotonin reuptake inhibitors, irrespective of their symptoms’ severity.
Some patients continue with a chronic or a chronic relapsing course.

correct_answer.text: The association between OCD and suicidality is weak.

correct_answers.text: The association between OCD and suicidality is weak.

questions.explanation: Contrary to this statement, OCD is associated with significant rates of suicidal ideation and attempts; the link is not weak.

questions.question_text: With regard to suicide and violence in schizophrenia, which of the following is incorrect?

options.text: Approximately 10% of patients with schizophrenia do commit suicide.
The prevalence of violence amongst outpatients with schizophrenia has been estimated to be 5%.
Suicide in schizophrenia usually occurs late into the illness.
Paranoid schizophrenics are more likely to commit suicide compared with other subtypes of schizophrenics.
Verbal aggression is the most common type of violence seen amongst schizophrenics.

correct_answer.text: Suicide in schizophrenia usually occurs late into the illness.

correct_answers.text: Suicide in schizophrenia usually occurs late into the illness.

questions.explanation: Suicide risk peaks early in the illness, not late.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old male with a history of schizophrenia presents to the outpatient clinic with prominent cognitive impairments. Which of the following would you recommend as an adjunct medication?
questions.explanation: Adjunctive cholinergic agents have been shown to marginally improve verbal learning and memory in schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: First-degree relatives of individuals with hyperkinetic disorder are particularly prone towards the development of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Family studies indicate an increased risk of bipolar disorder among first-degree relatives of children with ADHD.

questions.question_text: The mother of a 14-year-old boy with attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) wants to ask you about the side effects of methylphenidate medication. Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: Methylphenidate almost always delays physical growth.
A drug holiday is required to facilitate growth.
Methylphenidate combined with clonidine is better than placebo in controlling tics and ADHD symptoms.
Dependence is common in patients who continue methylphenidate long-term.

correct_answer.text: Dependence is common in patients who continue methylphenidate long-term.

correct_answers.text: Dependence is common in patients who continue methylphenidate long-term.

questions.explanation:
Most	patients	do	not	develop	dependence	on	methylphenidate	if	the	stimulant	is	used
over	the	long	term.	Electrocardiogram	should	be	checked	before	prescribing	methylphenidate	and
clonidine.	Methylphenidate	is	also	indicated	for	narcolepsy

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old woman suffering from schizophrenia has been well treated, and her last admission was 1 year ago. For the last month, she has been having symptoms of poor appetite, insomnia and feelings of hopelessness. The most likely diagnosis is
questions.explanation: Depressive symptoms emerging after stabilization of psychosis indicate post-schizophrenia depression rather than negative symptoms or schizoaffective disorder.

questions.question_text: With regard to the aetiology of depression in patients suffering from Parkinson disease, which of the following is least likely to be a predisposing factor?

options.text: Having a family history of depression
Low dopamine levels in the mesolimbic system

questions.explanation: Left-sided, not right-sided, brain lesions are associated with depression; right-sided injuries are less linked.

questions.question_text: A 13-year-old obese boy with learning disability has been referred to the learning disability clinic. His mother claimed that he has been having irresistible hunger drive associated with incessant skin picking. In addition, he also tends to talk to himself. Which other psychiatric comorbidity is highly prevalent in his condition?
questions.explanation: Prader–Willi syndrome is frequently comorbid with obsessive-compulsive behaviors such as skin picking.

questions.question_text: What is the estimated prevalence of schizophrenia in people with mental retardation?
questions.explanation: Studies estimate a 3%–5% prevalence of schizophrenia among individuals with intellectual disability.

questions.question_text: Hypermethylation of which of the following genes is most likely to be associated with antisocial personality disorder?
questions.explanation: Hypermethylation of the MAO-A promoter gene has been linked to antisocial personality traits.

questions.question_text: Approximately what percentage of elderly individuals suffer from major depressive disorder?
questions.explanation: Major depressive disorder affects about 3% of the elderly population.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a technique used in Moreno’s psychodrama?
questions.explanation: Moreno’s psychodrama techniques include role reversal—both reciprocal and representational—for experiential insight.

questions.question_text: A 29-year-old woman tells her psychotherapist that everything has been going well for her and that she is making good progress in her treatment. She leaves the therapy session and engages in self-harm. Which of the following best describes the above phenomenon?
questions.explanation: Acting out is the unconscious enactment of conflicts outside therapy rather than discussing them in session.

questions.question_text: Which one of the following statements regarding the standard error of the mean (SEM) is false?

options.text: As sample size increases, SEM decreases.
As the SD increases, SEM increases.
It is used in constructing confidence intervals for a mean or proportion.
It measures the variability of the sample statistic (mean or proportion) in relation to the true but unknown population characteristic.
It is a measure of the variability of the observations.

correct_answer.text: It is a measure of the variability of the observations.

correct_answers.text: It is a measure of the variability of the observations.

questions.explanation: SEM measures the variability of the sample mean across repeated samples, not the variability of individual observations (that is the SD).

questions.question_text: Which of the following regarding student’s t-test is false?

options.text: Calculated t-value is an observed difference in means/standard error of the difference in means.

Calculated t-value is compared with a critical t-value from tables at a predetermined significance level and appropriate degrees of freedom. The larger the value of t (±), the smaller the value of p and the stronger the evidence that the null hypothesis is untrue.
Independent sample t-test is used to compare the effects of two drugs on a particular patient at different points in time.
Paired t-tests compare the means of two small paired observations, either on the same individual or on the matched individual.
The SDs must be approximately the same in the two groups.

correct_answer.text: Independent sample t-test is used to compare the effects of two drugs on a particular patient at different points in time.

correct_answers.text: Independent sample t-test is used to compare the effects of two drugs on a particular patient at different points in time.

questions.explanation: Independent t-tests compare two different groups’ means; paired t-tests compare two measurements from the same or matched subjects over time.

questions.question_text: In a study to investigate the general public’s perspective on traditional Chinese medicine, participants are first identified based on certain characteristics and are then required to provide the names of other potential participants. What type of sampling method is this?
questions.explanation: Snowball sampling recruits initial subjects who then refer others, useful for hard-to-reach populations.

questions.question_text: A 36-year-old man is diagnosed with heroin dependence. Which of the following symptoms would he not develop tolerance to?
questions.explanation: Tolerance develops to many opioid effects (sedation, euphoria, respiratory depression) but not to constipation.

questions.question_text: A 21-year-old man was at a social event, and his friend offered him a recreational drug. He took the drug knowing that it would not cause physical withdrawal symptoms if he were to abruptly stop taking it subsequently. Which of the following is the most likely drug?
questions.explanation: LSD produces hallucinogenic effects but does not cause physical withdrawal symptoms on cessation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following antidepressants is the most appropriate if a patient has preexisting sexual dysfunction and has been referred to the National Health Service (NHS) mental health service for depression?
questions.explanation: Bupropion has a lower risk of sexual side effects than SSRIs and is preferable in patients with baseline sexual dysfunction.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old woman has been taking first-generation antipsychotic for her schizophrenia condition throughout her pregnancy. Which of the following would her infant be most susceptible to?
questions.explanation: Exposure to first-generation antipsychotics is associated with an increased risk of preterm birth.

questions.question_text: Which of the following genes has been found to be implicated in hyperkinetic disorder and has been linked to an enhanced response to psycho-stimulants?
questions.explanation: The DAT1 10-repeat allele has been associated with ADHD and better response to methylphenidate.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old woman has been having difficulties with sleep. Over the past couple of months, she has been frequently having the urge to move her legs as a result of unpleasant sensations while she is resting. At times, even with movement, there is no relief of her symptoms. She has decided to seek help from her general practitioner (GP). You would advise the GP to consider commencement of the following medications, with the exception of
questions.explanation: SSRIs like fluoxetine may worsen restless legs; treatments include dopaminergic agents, gabapentin, benzodiazepines and iron if deficient.

questions.question_text: With regard to paraphrenia, which of the following personality types is a predisposing factor?
questions.explanation: Long-standing paranoid personality traits may predispose to late-life paraphrenia.

questions.question_text: A 28-year-old university student presents to the emergency department with the following features: auditory hallucinations, visual hallucinations, paranoid delusions, thought disorders and passivity experiences. His room-mate informs you that the patient has been abusing drugs such as amphetamine lately. Which of the following clinical signs and symptoms would make you suspect that this is more likely to be substance-induced psychotic disorder versus that of an underlying schizophrenia?
questions.explanation: Visual hallucinations are more characteristic of substance-induced psychoses; thought disorder and passivity are more typical of primary schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: Based on the Randomized Injectable Opioid Treatment Trial (RIOTT), which of the following statements is correct?

options.text: Oral methadone treatment showed clear benefits over supervised injectable heroin in health and social outcomes.
Supervised injectable heroin treatment showed clear benefits over oral methadone in health and social outcomes.
Supervised injectable methadone treatment showed clear benefits over oral methadone in health and social outcomes.
Both supervised injectable heroin treatment and supervised injectable methadone treatment showed clear benefits over optimized oral methadone in health and social outcomes.
Neither supervised injectable heroin treatment nor supervised injectable methadone treatment showed benefits over optimized oral methadone in health and social outcomes.

correct_answer.text: Neither supervised injectable heroin treatment nor supervised injectable methadone treatment showed benefits over optimized oral methadone in health and social outcomes.

correct_answers.text: Neither supervised injectable heroin treatment nor supervised injectable methadone treatment showed benefits over optimized oral methadone in health and social outcomes.

questions.explanation: RIOTT found no clear benefit of supervised injectable heroin or injectable methadone over optimized oral methadone in health and social outcomes.

questions.question_text: Which of the following definitions is incorrect?

options.text: Absolute risk reduction is the difference in risk of a given event between two groups.
Confidence interval is the range of values within which one can be 95% certain that the true reference population value lies.
Number needed to treat is the number needed to treat to get one bad outcome.
Relative risk is the ratio of the risk of a given event in one group of subjects compared with another group.
Relative risk reduction is the proportion of the initial or baseline risk that was eliminated by a given treatment or by avoidance of exposure to a risk factor.

correct_answer.text: Number needed to treat is the number needed to treat to get one bad outcome.

correct_answers.text: Number needed to treat is the number needed to treat to get one bad outcome.

questions.explanation: Number needed to treat (NNT) refers to the number of patients who must be treated to prevent one additional bad outcome, not to cause one bad outcome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is false for case–control studies?

options.text: They are not ideal for rare diseases/outcomes.
They are poor for rare exposures.
Temporal relationships may be difficult to establish.

correct_answer.text: They are not ideal for rare diseases/outcomes.

correct_answers.text: They are not ideal for rare diseases/outcomes.

questions.explanation: Case–control studies are ideal for studying rare diseases or outcomes because they start with cases and compare exposures.

questions.question_text: Which of the following definitions best describes face validity?

options.text: How well a category appears to describe an illness.
How internally consistent a measure is.
How well a category predicts a pertinent aspect of care.
How often the same diagnosis is assigned by different assessors.
Whether a category has meaning in terms of what it is designed to describe.

correct_answer.text: How well a category appears to describe an illness.

correct_answers.text: How well a category appears to describe an illness.

questions.explanation: Face validity refers to whether a test or category superficially appears to measure or describe what it should.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best describes Cronbach’s alpha?

options.text: It determines whether a test measures what it purports to measure.
It indicates the internal consistency of the test.
It examines the extent of agreement between a present measurement and one in the future.
It describes the level of agreement between assessments of the same material made by two or more assessors at roughly the same time.
It is a measure of agreement in which allowance is made for chance agreement.

correct_answer.text: It indicates the internal consistency of the test.

correct_answers.text: It indicates the internal consistency of the test.

questions.explanation: Cronbach’s alpha measures the internal consistency (average inter-item correlation) of a test.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old woman suffering from schizophrenia has been taken haloperidol for the past 10 years. Her QTc is 500 ms. She wants to find out the potential medical complications if she continues to take haloperidol. Which of the following complications is least likely?
questions.explanation: QT prolongation primarily affects ventricular repolarization, leading to torsades and ventricular arrhythmias; atrial fibrillation is not linked.

questions.question_text: Which of the following symptoms is least likely to be different between young and old people suffering from depressive disorder?
questions.explanation: Sleep disturbance (insomnia, early awakening) is common in both younger and older depressed patients.

questions.question_text: For management of depression in old people, which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.text: Newer antidepressants such as SSRI and serotonin and norepinephrine reuptake inhibitors (SNRIs) are better tolerated as they have lesser side effects.
Tricyclic antidepressants are absolutely contraindicated in old people.
Depressed elderly presenting with delusion may require the addition of an antipsychotic.
Electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) is the most effective treatment for life-threatening depressive disorder.
Depressed elderly who show resistance to first-line treatment tend to do well with lithium augmentation.

correct_answer.text: Tricyclic antidepressants are absolutely contraindicated in old people.

correct_answers.text: Tricyclic antidepressants are absolutely contraindicated in old people.

questions.explanation: While tricyclics are used cautiously in the elderly, they are not absolutely contraindicated; they may still be prescribed if benefits outweigh risks.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is considered to be a good prognostic factor for elderly depression?

options.text: Active medical illness or poor physical health

questions.explanation: Female gender is associated with a better prognosis in late-life depression; the others predict chronicity or poorer outcome.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common cause of mental retardation?
questions.explanation: Down syndrome is the single most common cause of intellectual disability, accounting for about 30% of cases.

questions.question_text: What is the approximate proportion of people with Down syndrome at age 60–69 years who will develop Alzheimer’s disease?
questions.explanation: By age 60–69, approximately 60% of individuals with Down syndrome meet criteria for Alzheimer’s disease.

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old male has been admitted to the gastroenterology unit for hepatic dysfunction. He has been diagnosed with liver disease since he was a teenager. The core trainee has evaluated him and found that apart from him having depressed mood, he also has some elements of cognitive impairment. The medical team is particularly concerned currently about the neurological complications arising from his condition. Based on your knowledge, which of the following is the most likely modality of inheritance for the disease that this 22-year-old male has?
questions.explanation: Wilson disease is inherited in an autosomal-recessive manner, causing copper accumulation in liver and brain.

questions.question_text: Stress and depression often increase the risk of coronary artery disease (CAD). Which of the following biological markers is least likely to be involved?
questions.explanation: IL-10 is an anti-inflammatory cytokine, whereas stress and depression upregulate proinflammatory markers like IL-6, fibrinogen and vWF and alter NK cells.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding criminal behaviour in patients with schizophrenia is false?

options.text: It increases with comorbid substance use.
Patients with schizophrenia have higher rates of offending compared with the general population.
Patients with schizophrenia usually assault a known person rather than a stranger.
Violence is a common precipitant prior to the first admission to psychiatric ward.
Violence in patients with schizophrenia is not always a result of psychosis.

correct_answer.text: Patients with schizophrenia have higher rates of offending compared with the general population.

correct_answers.text: Patients with schizophrenia have higher rates of offending compared with the general population.

questions.explanation: Schizophrenia patients do NOT have a higher overall offending rate than the general population; rates mirror community levels, though substance use raises violence risk.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements regarding offending in patients with epilepsy is false?

options.text: Low intelligence is associated with violence in patients with epilepsies.
Offending in epileptics is usually during the ictal phase of the illness.
There is an approximately twofold increase in the prevalence of epilepsy in prisoners compared with the general population.
The rate and type of offending by those with epilepsy are similar to the general population.
There is no excess of violent crimes in epileptic prisoners.

correct_answer.text: Offending in epileptics is usually during the ictal phase of the illness.

correct_answers.text: Offending in epileptics is usually during the ictal phase of the illness.

questions.explanation: Violent crimes in epilepsy occur almost exclusively interictally, not during ictal seizures.

questions.question_text: What percentage of children with autism is also diagnosed with severe or profound mental retardation?
questions.explanation: About 70% of autistic children have intellectual disability; roughly 30% have mild–moderate and 50% severe–profound impairment.

questions.question_text: Previous research into the genetics associated with conduct disorder has demonstrated that conduct disorder is associated with the inheritance of antisocial traits from parents who demonstrate criminal behaviours. All of the following are biological factors that have been implicated in the aetiology of conduct disorder except
questions.explanation: Elevated, not low, testosterone has been linked to conduct disorder; the others have all been implicated.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old female has recently given birth to her son. After delivery, her husband noted that there has been a change in her personality and behaviour. She has been evaluated by the mental health team and has been admitted to the ward, as she is believed to be suffering from post-partum psychosis. The medical student attached to the team is curious: Which of the following is not a common clinical feature of post-partum psychosis?

options.text: Being either excessively withdrawn or elated and labile in mood
Presence of mood-incongruent delusions of reference and persecution

questions.explanation: First-rank schizophrenia symptoms (e.g. thought insertion) are uncommon in post-partum psychosis, which more often shows mood incongruence, catatonia and hallucinations.

questions.question_text: Which of the following forensic offences is most highly associated with individuals diagnosed with Asperger syndrome?
questions.explanation: Studies have found fire-setting behaviour disproportionately in offenders with Asperger’s, likely related to social cognition deficits.

questions.question_text: Based on the findings of the Multimodal Treatment of Attention Deficit Hyperactivity Disorder (MTA) Study, which of the following is true with regard to the incidence of substance abuse in children with ADHD?
questions.explanation: The MTA cohort showed around a two-fold higher rate of subsequent substance abuse compared to peers.

questions.question_text: A 55-year-old female has been diagnosed with breast cancer recently, has undergone surgery and is currently now on tamoxifen. If her mood is low, which antidepressant could she be started on, with minimal interactions with tamoxifen?
questions.explanation: Venlafaxine has minimal CYP2D6 inhibition and thus preserves tamoxifen metabolism better than SSRIs like paroxetine or fluoxetine.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old man has been brought into the emergency department. He is noted to have increased heart rate, associated with euphoria and hyperactivity. His friends, who have accompanied him, informed that he has been abusing khat for the past year. Which of the following is not a complication associated with chronic usage?
questions.explanation: Chronic khat use is linked to depression, psychosis, cardiovascular risk and reduced libido; it does not reduce suicidal thoughts.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is false?

options.text: Routine investigations include U & Es, liver function tests, serum calcium and phosphate.
In patients with suspected hypoparathyroidism, 25(OH)D3 is a reliable indicator of total body stores of vitamin D.
Chronic hypocalcaemia causes alopecia, cataracts and papilloedema.
Treatment of hypoparathyroidism involves a combination of alfacalcidol and calcitriol.
The multiple endocrine neoplasia type I (MEN 1) syndrome involves parathyroid tumour, pituitary adenoma and phaeochromocytoma.

correct_answer.text: The multiple endocrine neoplasia type I (MEN 1) syndrome involves parathyroid tumour, pituitary adenoma and phaeochromocytoma.

correct_answers.text: The multiple endocrine neoplasia type I (MEN 1) syndrome involves parathyroid tumour, pituitary adenoma and phaeochromocytoma.

questions.explanation: MEN1 characteristically involves parathyroid, pancreatic islet and pituitary tumours; phaeochromocytoma is part of MEN2.

questions.question_text: Which of the following statements best describes criterion validity?

options.text: It refers to predictive and concurrent validity together.
It refers to face and content validity together.
It refers to convergent and divergent validity together.
It refers to construct validity and predictive validity together.
It refers to the level of agreement between assessments by one rater of the same material at two or more different times.

correct_answer.text: It refers to predictive and concurrent validity together.

correct_answers.text: It refers to predictive and concurrent validity together.

questions.explanation: Criterion validity assesses how well a measure correlates with a gold-standard outcome, encompassing predictive and concurrent validity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following represents a technique of randomization such that contamination between intervention and control group is being minimized?
questions.explanation: Cluster randomization assigns intact groups (e.g. clinics) to arms, reducing risk that individuals in different conditions will interact and contaminate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following studies produces Figure 1.1?
questions.explanation: Forest plots comparing effect sizes across studies are produced by meta-analyses.

questions.question_text: Based on Figure 1.1, which of the following studies has the largest sample size?

options.text: There is no difference in sample size between studies.

questions.explanation: The size of the square in a forest plot is proportional to sample size; Yen et al. (2009) has the largest square.

questions.question_text: In Figure 1.1, the odds ratio is indicated for each study. Which of the following is the correct formula for odds ratio?

options.text: (The number of controls without ADHD times the number of controls with ADHD)/(The number of IA participants with ADHD times the number of IA without ADHD)
(The number of controls with ADHD times the number of IA without ADHD)/(The number of IA participants with ADHD times the number of controls without ADHD)
(The number of IA participants with ADHD times the number of controls with ADHD)/(The number of controls without ADHD times the number of IA without ADHD)
(The number of IA participants with ADHD times the number of controls without ADHD)/(The number of controls with ADHD times the number of IA without ADHD)
(The number of IA participants with ADHD times the number of IA without ADHD)/(The number of controls without ADHD times the number of controls with ADHD)

correct_answer.text: (The number of IA participants with ADHD times the number of controls without ADHD)/(The number of controls with ADHD times the number of IA without ADHD)

correct_answers.text: (The number of IA participants with ADHD times the number of controls without ADHD)/(The number of controls with ADHD times the number of IA without ADHD)

questions.explanation: In a 2×2 table (IA vs controls × ADHD vs no ADHD), OR= (IA+ADHD × Control–ADHD)/(Control+ADHD × IA–ADHD).

questions.question_text: Referring to the study conducted by Yoo et al. (2009) in Figure 1.1, there is a horizontal line drawing across the box. What is represented by the horizontal line?

options.text: Interquartile range of the odds ratio in the study conducted by Yoo et al. (2009)
Interquartile range of the standardized mean differences in severity of ADHD between IA and controls
95% confidence interval of the odds ratio
95% confidence interval of the standardized mean differences in severity of ADHD between IA and controls
99% confidence interval of the standardized mean differences in severity of ADHD between IA and controls

correct_answer.text: 95% confidence interval of the odds ratio

correct_answers.text: 95% confidence interval of the odds ratio

questions.explanation: The horizontal line through each square on a forest plot denotes the 95% confidence interval of that study’s effect estimate.

questions.question_text: Based on Figure 1.1, what is the estimated heterogeneity between different studies?

options.text: There is not enough information provided to determine where there is heterogeneity or not.
There is significant but low level of heterogeneity.
There is significant but moderate level of heterogeneity.
There is significant but high level of heterogeneity.

questions.explanation: All study confidence intervals overlap a common vertical line; this suggests no statistically significant heterogeneity.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the correct conclusion drawn from Figure 1.1?

options.text: People suffering from ADHD are less likely to develop IA compared with controls.
People suffering from ADHD are more likely to develop IA compared with controls.
People suffering from IA are less likely to develop ADHD compared with controls.
People suffering from IA are more likely to develop ADHD compared with controls.
There is no difference between patients suffering from IA and controls in the risk of the developing ADHD.

correct_answer.text: People suffering from IA are more likely to develop ADHD compared with controls.

correct_answers.text: People suffering from IA are more likely to develop ADHD compared with controls.

questions.explanation: An overall odds ratio >1 indicates that IA sufferers have a higher likelihood of comorbid ADHD than controls.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a sign of resistance in psychoanalysis?

options.text: Blurting things out without censoring them

correct_answer.text: Blurting things out without censoring them

correct_answers.text: Blurting things out without censoring them

questions.explanation: Blurting out uncensored thoughts is a hallmark of free association, not resistance; the others are classic signs of resistance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a mature defence mechanism?
questions.explanation: Anticipation—realistically planning for future discomfort—is considered a mature defence; the others are less mature defences.

questions.question_text: The following are features of pseudo-dementia, with the exception of

options.text: Presence of lack of motivation and does not attempt to answer the questions
Memory deficits are often reported by others

correct_answer.text: Memory deficits are often reported by others

correct_answers.text: Memory deficits are often reported by others

questions.explanation: In pseudo-dementia (depression mimicking dementia), patients themselves complain of memory loss, whereas in true dementia relatives report the deficits.

questions.question_text: All of the following are common clinical symptoms found in the elderly with mania, except
questions.explanation: Elderly manic patients often have slowed or circumstantial thinking rather than rapid flight of ideas.

questions.question_text: Down syndrome is a condition that is caused usually by trisomy 21. Investigators have made use of techniques that induce X-chromosome inactivation to silence the activity of the extra gene. Which of the following is the correct terminology for such a process/technique?
questions.explanation: Lyonization refers to X-chromosome inactivation, named after geneticist Mary Lyon.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of Rett syndrome?
questions.explanation: Rett syndrome features small hands/feet, not hypertrophic feet; the other listed signs are characteristic.

questions.question_text: You are a doctor working in the British Army and encounter soldiers who develop post-concussion symptoms after head injury. Which of the following factors are most significant predisposing factors for post-concussion symptoms amongst soldiers?

options.text: Depression and injury occur during military operation
Depression and severity of body injury
Injury occurs during military operation and severity of body injury
Post-traumatic stress and severity of body injury

questions.explanation: Studies identify comorbid depression and PTSD as the strongest predictors of persistent post-concussion symptoms.

questions.question_text: Approximately what percentage of patients eventually kill themselves in 1 year following deliberate self-harm (DSH)?
questions.explanation: About 1% of DSH patients die by suicide within the first year after the episode.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not used to treat sexual offenders?
questions.explanation: Anti-libidinal agents (cyproterone, medroxyprogesterone, SSRIs) are used; exogenous testosterone would increase libido.

questions.question_text: During a forensic assessment of an accused who has recently committed rape, he tells the forensic psychiatrist that he did it on impulse. When he was asked about whether he considered the potential consequences, he denied doing so. He also has had a history of poor work record and has used heroin in the past. Based on the classification of rapists by Trick et al. (1981), he will be classified as
questions.explanation: Sociopathic (impulsive) rapists act with little planning, often with antisocial traits and substance use history.

questions.question_text: Based on the Isle of Wight study, the age of onset of oppositional defiant disorder is before
questions.explanation: ODD typically emerges before age 8 years.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications is most effective in treating aggression in conduct disorder based on recent research?
questions.explanation: Meta-analyses support risperidone as the most consistently effective antipsychotic for aggression in CD.

questions.question_text: A 13-year-old boy has dropped out from secondary school. He is odd and is not accepted by his classmates. Your consultant recommends ruling out Asperger’s syndrome. Which of the following features would not support such a diagnosis?

options.text: Worries about the welfare of his classmates

questions.explanation: Asperger’s by definition does not include language delay; speech milestones are usually normal.

questions.question_text: With regard to the treatment of OCD, poor prognostic factors include all of the following, with the exception of

options.text: Symptoms involving the need for symmetry and exactness
Predominance of phobic ruminative ideas, with the absence of compulsions

correct_answer.text: Predominance of phobic ruminative ideas, with the absence of compulsions

correct_answers.text: Predominance of phobic ruminative ideas, with the absence of compulsions

questions.explanation: Predominant phobic rumination without compulsions tends to have a better response and thus is not a poor prognostic sign.

questions.question_text: All of the following are known to be risk factors for suicide, except
questions.explanation: Suicide risk is elevated at low and high SES extremes but lower in the middle social class.

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old man presents to the clinic with white patches and gingival fibromata. He attends a special school because of learning difficulties and receives medical outpatient follow-up for epilepsy. A whole body scan shows tumours in the spleen, kidney and lungs. Which of the following conditions does he have?
questions.explanation: Tuberous sclerosis presents with hypomelanotic macules, facial angiofibromas, epilepsy and multiple hamartomas in various organs.

questions.question_text: What has been the estimated prevalence of mania in elderly?
questions.explanation: Mania in the elderly accounts for about 5% of geriatric psychiatric admissions.

questions.question_text: A patient with anxiety disorder is keen to go for hypnotherapy to relieve her symptoms. Which of the following statements about hypnotherapy is correct?

options.text: Evidence shows that hypnosis can help recall in psychotherapy, leading to better outcomes.
It is superior to relaxation exercises.
It is recommended in the National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (NICE) guidelines for treatment of anxiety disorders.
Sudden removal of symptoms by suggestion under hypnosis can lead to rebound depression and anxiety.
Suggestion with hypnosis is found to be superior to suggestion without hypnosis.

correct_answer.text: Sudden removal of symptoms by suggestion under hypnosis can lead to rebound depression and anxiety.

correct_answers.text: Sudden removal of symptoms by suggestion under hypnosis can lead to rebound depression and anxiety.

questions.explanation: Rapid symptom removal under hypnosis may precipitate rebound distress; there is limited evidence for superiority over other modalities.

questions.question_text: A medical student wants to look at the number of outpatients who experience postural hypotension with chlorpromazine treatment versus those who are not on treatment. Which of the following statistical tests is most appropriate in comparing the two groups?
questions.explanation:
Student’s	t-test	is	a	significance	test	used	to	compare	the	means	of	two	independent
different	sample	populations;	often	one	group	is	the	experimental	group	and	the	other	is	the	control.	It
is	a	parametric	test	that	assumes	the	samples	are	normally	distributed.	Paired	t-test	is	used	for	matched
studies	(e.g.	case–control	trials	and	matched-pair	randomized	controlled	trials).	In	Z-test,	an
observation	from	a	population	may	be	converted	into	a	standard	normal	deviate	(also	called	a	z-score),
which	is	the	number	of	SDs	that	separates	the	observation	from	the	mean	of	the	population.	In	one
way	analysis	of	variance	(ANOVA),	a	sample	of	individuals	from	a	number	of	different	populations	is
compared	with	some	outcome	measure	of	interest.	The	total	variance	in	the	observations	is	partitioned
into	a	part	due	to	differences	between	the	group	means	and	a	part	due	to	differences	between	subjects
in	the	same	group.	The	results	of	this	division	are	usually	arranged	in	an	ANOVA	table.

questions.question_text: A core trainee is seeing a 27-year-old woman in the specialist clinic. He gathers from her that she has an ideal weight she is aiming for and that she purges to lose weight. Which of the following would be more indicative and characteristic for diagnosing her with bulimia instead of anorexia?

options.text: Restriction of energy and food intake leading to a significantly low body weight
Persistent behaviour that interferes with weight gain
Poor impulse control with persistent preoccupation with eating and an irresistible craving for food

correct_answer.text: Poor impulse control with persistent preoccupation with eating and an irresistible craving for food

correct_answers.text: Poor impulse control with persistent preoccupation with eating and an irresistible craving for food

questions.explanation: Bulimia is typified by recurrent binge eating with lack of impulse control, followed by compensatory behaviours, despite normal or above-normal weight.

questions.question_text: A researcher wants to compare the effectiveness of asenepine treatment versus CBT in treatment of borderline personality disorder. Subjects are randomized into two groups. The first group will be administered asenapine for 12 weeks, after which they will be administered CBT for 12 weeks. The second group will undergo the reverse. Subjects will be given questionnaires to complete at the first and second 12th week. What type of study design is this?
questions.explanation: In a crossover design, participants receive both interventions in sequence, serving as their own controls.

questions.question_text: Based on the current literature, which of the following is not one of the recommended non-stimulant medications that are indicated for ADHD?
questions.explanation: Duloxetine is not routinely recommended for ADHD; the others have evidence as non-stimulant options.

questions.question_text: Approximately what percentage of young people with conduct disorder eventually develops dissocial personality disorder?
questions.explanation: Around 40% of adolescents with conduct disorder go on to meet criteria for antisocial (dissocial) personality disorder.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common psychiatric condition associated with Cushing syndrome?
questions.explanation: Depression affects 50–80% of patients with Cushing’s syndrome and is the most frequent neuropsychiatric manifestation.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a feature of Cornelia De Lange syndrome?
questions.explanation: Cornelia De Lange syndrome typically presents with severe-to-profound intellectual disability rather than mild-to-moderate.

questions.question_text: Which of the following tools is not used for predicting sex offence recidivism?

options.text: Rapid Risk Assessment for Sex Offence Recidivism (RRASOR)

questions.explanation: VRAG assesses general violence risk, not specifically sexual reoffending.

questions.question_text: If lithium is started in an elderly with mania, what is the maximum recommended total daily dose based on the current treatment guidelines?
questions.explanation: In frail elderly, lithium dosing is lower than in younger adults, with a maximum of about 600 mg per day recommended.

questions.question_text: Your patient is a 15-year-old girl who has a history of repeated DSH and a poor relationship with her parents. You are keen to start her on family therapy. However, her parents are busy with their work, and they prefer family therapy that focuses on presenting communication difficulties with less frequent sessions. Which one of the following types of family therapy would you recommend?
questions.explanation: Eclectic family therapy concentrates on present communication patterns, is flexible in session frequency and addresses immediate relational issues.

questions.question_text: A 40-year-old alcoholic has been referred by his local GP to the addiction service. He has been drinking at least eight bottles of beer on a daily basis for the past 8 years. He has tried to stop drinking previously but relapsed due to the strong cravings that he had. Which of the following medications would help him deal with his strong cravings?
questions.explanation: Naltrexone, an opioid antagonist, reduces alcohol craving by blocking reward pathways.

questions.question_text: A 34-year-old woman arrives at the emergency department with euphoria, visual hallucinations, arrhythmias, nausea and diaphoresis. Which of the following substances is she likely to be intoxicated with?
questions.explanation: Cocaine intoxication produces euphoria, hallucinations, diaphoresis, tachyarrhythmias and sympathomimetic signs.

questions.question_text: Which of the following defence mechanisms is associated with phobias?
questions.explanation: Repression—pushing distressing thoughts out of awareness—is commonly seen in phobic avoidance.

questions.question_text: Which of the following medications does not need to be held off at the time of ECT to ensure successful treatment?
questions.explanation: SSRIs like fluoxetine need not be discontinued for ECT; bupropion and clozapine raise seizure risk, and lithium may prolong seizures or cause delirium.

questions.question_text: Which of the following disorders is not associated with 5HTT gene polymorphisms?
questions.explanation: 5HTT polymorphisms have been linked to mood disorders, OCD, autism and anxiety traits—but not consistently to ADHD.

questions.question_text: Which part of brain dysfunction has been suggested to be implicated in OCD?
questions.explanation: Functional and structural studies implicate fronto–striatal circuits, especially basal ganglia, in OCD pathophysiology.

questions.question_text: A medical student wants to study whether cannabis is a risk factor for the development of schizophrenia. He plans to survey 100 patients with schizophrenia and 100 age-matched controls with regard to their cannabis usage history. What type of study is this?
questions.explanation: Case–control studies compare past exposures (cannabis use) in a group with the outcome (schizophrenia) versus controls.

questions.question_text: An elderly woman suffers from somatoform pain disorder, and her son wants to find out from you whether this condition is common in the community. What is the 1-year prevalence of this condition?
questions.explanation: The 1-year prevalence of somatoform pain disorder is about 8%.

questions.question_text: A 35-year-old woman presents with a major depressive episode with a background of borderline personality disorder. You are keen to start her on treatment. Which of the following is true?

options.text: Cognitive behavioural therapy is more effective than medication.
Cognitive behavioural therapy is more effective than interpersonal psychotherapy.
Interpersonal psychotherapy is more effective than cognitive behavioural therapy.
Neither cognitive behavioural therapy nor interpersonal psychotherapy is effective.
Only medication is required, and there is no need for psychological treatment.

correct_answer.text: Cognitive behavioural therapy is more effective than interpersonal psychotherapy.

correct_answers.text: Cognitive behavioural therapy is more effective than interpersonal psychotherapy.

questions.explanation: Evidence shows CBT is more effective than IPT for depression comorbid with borderline personality traits.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is the most common neuropsychiatric condition that usually arises from Addison disease?
questions.explanation: Memory problems are the most frequent neuropsychiatric manifestation in adrenal insufficiency.

questions.question_text: A 49-year-old man refuses to see the registrar at the clinic and insists on seeing the consultant psychiatrist. He declares that he is an important person and has no time for young doctors. He insists on seeing the psychiatrist immediately. He tells the psychiatrist he will soon be one of the top in his profession and will have hundreds of employees’ fates in his hands.

options.text: Emotionally unstable personality disorder, borderline type

questions.explanation: Narcissistic personality disorder features grandiosity, entitlement and need for special treatment.

questions.question_text: A 27-year-old woman enjoys being the centre of attention and dresses seductively to draw the attention she wants. She has had multiple relationships, each lasting from a few days to a few months and none lasting more than 6 months. She bursts out crying when describing her past relationships and laughs as she reminisces about the happier times.

options.text: Emotionally unstable personality disorder, borderline type

questions.explanation: Histrionic personality disorder involves attention-seeking, dramatic emotional displays and superficial relationships.

questions.question_text: A 37-year-old woman has had several suicide attempts, each prompted by quarrels with her boyfriend. She uses suicidal threats whenever her boyfriend suggests breaking up with her. She has changed psychiatrists three times over the past year as she thinks they are not concerned enough about her.

options.text: Emotionally unstable personality disorder, borderline type

correct_answer.text: Emotionally unstable personality disorder, borderline type

correct_answers.text: Emotionally unstable personality disorder, borderline type

questions.explanation: Borderline (emotionally unstable) personality disorder is marked by impulsive self-harm, unstable relationships and fear of abandonment.

questions.question_text: List one of Yalom’s therapeutic factors in group therapy.
questions.explanation: Yalom’s factors include universality, altruism, catharsis, cohesiveness, etc.; catharsis is the shared expression of emotion.

questions.question_text: The founder of group analysis who propounded the idea of a social matrix.
questions.explanation: S. H. Foulkes developed group analysis and introduced the concept of the social matrix.

questions.question_text: List one of Bion’s three basic assumptions.
questions.explanation: Bion’s three basic assumptions in groups are dependency, fight–flight and pairing.

questions.question_text: The body mass index (BMI) of patients with schizophrenia in the outpatient psychosis clinic.
questions.explanation: BMI is measured on a continuous scale with no fixed categories.

questions.question_text: The temperature of the psychiatric ward in Fahrenheit.
questions.explanation: Fahrenheit has equal intervals but an arbitrary zero, making it an interval scale.

questions.question_text: The ethnicity of patients in a suicide research study.
questions.explanation: Ethnicity is a categorical (nominal) variable with no inherent ordering.

questions.question_text: The temperature of the psychiatric ward in Kelvin.
questions.explanation: Kelvin has a true zero point and consistent intervals, making it a ratio scale.

questions.question_text: Hamilton Rating Scale for Depression (HAM-D) score <11 = mild depression = ‘1’.
questions.explanation: Coding HAM-D categories as 1,2,... is an ordinal scale—ranked but unequal intervals.

questions.question_text: A researcher wishes to perform a study to assess the effect of exercise on stress levels and mental health. He places his advertisements for subject participation outside a gym. He subsequently receives many interested participants, who happen to be members of that gym.
questions.explanation: Volunteer bias arises when those who choose to participate differ systematically from non-volunteers.

questions.question_text: A psychiatrist is conducting a randomized controlled trial studying the effects of placebo and antidepressants. He is concerned about his depressed patients and decides to place those with higher depression scores in the group receiving antidepressants.
questions.explanation: By overriding random assignment to benefit certain patients, this introduces selection bias.

questions.question_text: A researcher conducts a retrospective study to compare patients with schizophrenia and normal controls to identify risk factors for schizophrenia. He finds that these patients smoked a lot before the onset of their symptoms. He then concludes that smoking leads to schizophrenia.
questions.explanation: Ascertainment bias can occur when data collection differs between groups, leading to spurious exposure–outcome links.

questions.question_text: Phencyclidine. (Choose one option for detection in urine.)
questions.explanation: Phencyclidine (PCP) can be detected in urine for up to 8 days.

questions.question_text: Ecstasy. (Choose one option for detection in urine.)
questions.explanation: MDMA (ecstasy) is typically detectable in urine for around 48 hours.

questions.question_text: Amphetamine. (Choose one option for detection in urine.)
questions.explanation: Amphetamine metabolites are usually detectable for up to 48 hours in urine.

questions.question_text: Lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD). (Choose one option for detection in urine.)
questions.explanation: LSD is detectable in urine for up to 24 hours.

questions.question_text: A 75-year-old man presents with cognitive impairment, fluctuating consciousness and visual hallucinations. On physical examination, he has hypertonia and hypersalivation. The MMSE score is 18/20. His symptoms worsen after he is started on a low dose of risperidone. Which imaging technique is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Dopamine transporter imaging (DaTSCAN) helps distinguish Lewy body dementia (reduced striatal uptake) from other dementias.

questions.question_text: An 82-year-old woman presents with fluctuating, progressive memory loss and emotional incontinence. She has a history of falls and multiple medical problems, including old strokes, hypertension and diabetes. Her family says her personality is preserved. Which imaging technique is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Perfusion SPECT (HMPAO) can demonstrate patchy cortical perfusion defects characteristic of vascular dementia.

questions.question_text: A 25-year-old woman complained of vomiting, vertigo and bilateral numbness of the hands 2 years ago. These symptoms lasted for 1 month before she recovered, albeit gradually. Her numbness subsequently relapsed a few months later and spread to weakness of all four limbs to the extent that she is unable to balance herself. She is also suffering from increasing muscle spasms affecting mainly the lower limbs. There is urgency of micturition and diplopia. Which imaging technique is most appropriate?
questions.explanation: Multiple sclerosis is best evaluated by MRI showing white-matter plaques.

questions.question_text: Angelman syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Angelman syndrome features ataxia with characteristic hand-flapping movements.

questions.question_text: Down syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Down syndrome features a single palmar (simian) crease and almond-shaped palpebral fissures.

questions.question_text: Cri du chat syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Cri du chat patients have a high-pitched, cat-like cry in infancy.

questions.question_text: Smith–Magenis syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Smith–Magenis syndrome is marked by self-hugging behavior and a hoarse, deep voice.

questions.question_text: Patau syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Patau syndrome shows overlapping of the fingers over the thumb.

questions.question_text: Williams syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Williams syndrome features ‘elfin’ facies and often social disinhibition.

questions.question_text: Turner syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Turner syndrome is characterized by short stature and webbed neck.

questions.question_text: Tuberous sclerosis. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Tuberous sclerosis features hamartomatous tumours in brain, skin and organs.

questions.question_text: Di George syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Di George syndrome often includes cleft palate with conotruncal cardiac defects.

questions.question_text: Edwards syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Edwards syndrome (trisomy 18) is marked by rocker-bottom feet deformity.

questions.question_text: Lesch–Nyhan syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Lesch–Nyhan syndrome includes self-mutilation, dystonia and choreoathetoid movements.

questions.question_text: Klinefelter syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Klinefelter syndrome (47,XXY) presents with tall stature and small firm testicles.

questions.question_text: Prader–Willi syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

correct_answer.text: Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

correct_answers.text: Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

questions.explanation: Prader–Willi syndrome features hyperphagia leading to obesity and compulsive skin picking.

questions.question_text: Wolf–Hirschhorn syndrome. (Choose one characteristic clinical feature.)

options.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face
Excessive weight gain and skin pricking

correct_answer.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face

correct_answers.text: Down-turned fishlike mouth with Greek warrior helmet face

questions.explanation: Wolf–Hirschhorn syndrome patients show a ‘Greek warrior helmet’ facial appearance, with a down-turned mouth.

questions.question_text: Based on the ICD-10 criteria, what is the lower IQ limit for mild learning disability?
questions.explanation: Mild intellectual disability is defined by an IQ in the range 50–69; 50 is the lower bound.

questions.question_text: Based on the ICD-10 criteria, what is the lower IQ limit for moderate learning disability?
questions.explanation: Moderate intellectual disability corresponds to IQ 35–49; 35 is the lower limit.

questions.question_text: Based on the ICD-10 criteria, what is the lower IQ limit for severe learning disability?
questions.explanation: Severe intellectual disability is IQ 20–34; 20 is the lower bound.

questions.question_text: A 30-year-old man has been receiving treatment for schizophrenia over the past 3 years. He is currently stable and plans to get married and start a family. He is concerned about the genetic risks of schizophrenia in his offspring. The risk of schizophrenia in his child if his wife does not have schizophrenia is
questions.explanation: When one parent has schizophrenia, the lifetime risk in offspring is approximately 10%–14%.

questions.question_text: The risk of schizophrenia in his child if his wife has schizophrenia.
questions.explanation: When both parents have schizophrenia the offspring risk rises to about 36%–50%.

questions.question_text: The risk of schizophrenia if he adopts a child with velocardiofacial syndrome.
questions.explanation: Velocardiofacial (22q11 deletion) syndrome carries roughly a 24% risk of schizophrenia.

questions.question_text: The risk of schizophrenia in his half-sibling.
questions.explanation: Half-siblings share 25% of genes; risk is under 4%.

questions.question_text: The risk of schizophrenia in his younger cousin.
questions.explanation: First cousins have an approximate 2%–4% risk.

questions.question_text: The risk of schizophrenia in his nephews or nieces.
questions.explanation: The risk in nieces/nephews is similar to that for first cousins (~3%).

questions.question_text: The risk of schizophrenia in his biological uncles or aunts.
questions.explanation: Uncles/aunts carry about a 2.4% risk, under 4%.

questions.question_text: The percentage of people with schizophrenia who smoke.
questions.explanation: About 80%–85% of individuals with schizophrenia smoke.

questions.question_text: The percentage of people with schizophrenia who do not continue with antipsychotic medication after 1 year.
questions.explanation: Approximately 74% (70%–75%) discontinue their antipsychotic within one year.

questions.question_text: Which one is the most common and prevalent obsession?

options.text: Fear of illness, germs or bodily fear

questions.explanation: Contamination fears occur in ~45% of OCD patients, the highest prevalence.

questions.question_text: Which one is the most common and prevalent compulsion?
questions.explanation: Checking compulsions are seen in ~63%, the most prevalent compulsion.

questions.question_text: Which one is the least prevalent obsession?

options.text: Fear of illness, germs or bodily fear

questions.explanation: Intrusive sexual or aggressive thoughts occur in ~28%, the lowest among listed obsession types.

questions.question_text: Which one is the least prevalent compulsion?
questions.explanation: Counting compulsions (~36%) are less common than checking or washing.

questions.question_text: The usage of SSRIs for the treatment of depressive disorders in pregnancy could lead to which of the above abnormalities? (Choose four options.)
questions.explanation: SSRI exposure is linked to neonatal persistent pulmonary hypertension, preterm birth, lower birth weight and increased risk of miscarriage.

questions.question_text: Paroxetine is contraindicated for usage in pregnancy due to the potential for it inducing which one of the above abnormalities? (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Paroxetine use in the first trimester carries a higher risk of congenital cardiovascular defects.

questions.question_text: The usage of paroxetine and venlafaxine in pregnancy for the treatment of depressive disorder has been linked to the development of which one of the above abnormalities? (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Neonatal withdrawal syndrome (agitation, irritability) is reported with late‐pregnancy SSRI/SNRI exposure.

questions.question_text: The usage of lithium in pregnancy has been linked to the development of which one of the above abnormalities? (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Lithium exposure is associated with increased risk of Ebstein’s anomaly (a heart defect).

questions.question_text: The usage of valproate in pregnancy might lead to the development of which one of the above abnormalities? (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Valproate carries a well‐documented risk of neural tube defects (~1 in 100).

questions.question_text: Lamotrigine is a medication that requires further evaluation as it is not routinely used in pregnancy. It might result in the development of which one of the above abnormalities? (Choose one option.)
questions.explanation: Emerging data suggest lamotrigine may carry a small risk of oral clefts.

questions.question_text: A 12-year-old male has just been involved in a fight with his classmates. He has been quite defiant towards his parents, and they are struggling to cope with his behaviours. He does not have any psychiatric history. Which intervention is recommended?

options.text: Duty to inform the police if not reported yet
Obtain informed consent from the child and his or her parents

questions.explanation: Parent management training is the first-line psychosocial intervention for defiant behaviour in children without other diagnoses.

questions.question_text: A 16-year-old boy’s parents have taken a court order against him as he has been physically aggressive towards them and others.
