He was offered a course of psychotherapy, but his parents did not find the psychological intervention helpful. Which pharmacotherapy treatment is likely to be helpful for his condition?

options.text: Duty to inform the police if not reported yet
Obtain informed consent from the child and his or her parents

questions.explanation: Risperidone has evidence for reducing aggression in adolescents with conduct issues.

questions.question_text: A core trainee consults the consultant as he has received a request from a GP with regard to the forensic evaluation of a 15-year-old male who has been involved in a criminal activity.

options.text: Duty to inform the police if not reported yet
Obtain informed consent from the child and his or her parents

correct_answer.text: Duty to inform the police if not reported yet

correct_answers.text: Duty to inform the police if not reported yet
Obtain informed consent from the child and his or her parents

questions.explanation: For a forensic evaluation of a minor, obtain informed consent from both the child and parents.

questions.question_text: A core trainee has been tasked to assess a 15-year-old boy. He has been recently arrested by the police for setting fire to a school. He has been previously arrested for shoplifting as well as fights. Which intervention has strongest evidence to reduce reoffending?

options.text: Duty to inform the police if not reported yet
Obtain informed consent from the child and his or her parents

questions.explanation: Multisystemic therapy has been shown to reduce recidivism in serious juvenile offenders.

questions.question_text: A 7-year-old boy has been having frequent loss of temper. This has lead to arguments with parents, and he is irritable only at home and not at school. Which of the following is recommended?

options.text: Duty to inform the police if not reported yet
Obtain informed consent from the child and his or her parents

questions.explanation: Parent management training is effective for oppositional defiant behaviours confined to home.

questions.question_text: A 75-year-old man presents with cognitive impairment, fluctuating levels of consciousness, particularly confusion and bizarre behaviour in the evenings. His daughter claims that he has been seeing ghosts and not able to turn in his bed. On physical examination, he is found to have hypertonia and hypersalivation. The score on MMSE is 15/30. These above symptoms worsen following the commencement of antipsychotic medication. Which imaging technique?
questions.explanation: Findings are typical of Lewy body dementia; DaTSCAN shows reduced striatal uptake.

questions.question_text: An 80-year-old man presents with fluctuating, progressive memory loss and emotional incontinence. He has history of falls and is being treated for hypertension by his GP. His relatives say that his personality is preserved. Which imaging technique?
questions.explanation: Vascular dementia features patchy cortical perfusion defects best seen on perfusion SPECT.

questions.question_text: A 22-year-old woman complained of vertigo, vomiting and numbness of both hands 3 years ago. These symptoms lasted a month and she recovered fully, albeit gradually. She remained well until 8 months later when she had numbness of both hands and the left leg. These conditions improved spontaneously after 2 weeks. Twelve months after the initial symptoms, she again had numbness of both hands, but this time also with weakness of all four limbs so that she became chair-bound because she could not balance herself. She also suffered from increasing muscle spasm affecting mainly the lower limbs. There was also urgency of micturition and diplopia. Which imaging technique?
questions.explanation: The relapsing neurological deficits point to multiple sclerosis, best imaged with MRI.

questions.question_text: A 6-year-old boy is put in a maze to look for the toy box. After a few trials, he learns the cognitive map of the maze and needs a shorter time to find the toy box.
questions.explanation: He acquires a cognitive map without reinforcement—this is latent learning.

questions.question_text: A 2-year-old child is undergoing toilet training. The complex behaviour is broken down into simpler steps. She is rewarded with a sticker if she informs her mother when she has the urge to urinate. The positive reinforcement continues until she can inform her mother reliably without failures. Then the contingencies are altered, and she needs to go to the toilet on her own before the sticker is given.
questions.explanation: Chaining breaks a complex task into smaller steps, reinforcing each in sequence.

questions.question_text: A patient with moderate learning disability has an aggressive tendency and tends to assault other residents in the hostel. The staff have devised a plan in response to his aggressive behaviour. His main pleasurable activity is watching television. He will be removed from the TV room and put in a single room for a 2-hour time-out period if he assaults any resident.
questions.explanation: Penalty (time-out) removes a positive stimulus (TV) contingent on aggressive behaviour.

questions.question_text: Gathering evidence that long-term prevention goals are met.
questions.explanation: Follow-up studies assess whether long-term prevention outcomes have been achieved.

questions.question_text: Identifying prevention targets by gathering evidence for the suspected vulnerability of a specific target group.
questions.explanation: Prevalence rates help identify high-risk groups for targeted prevention.

questions.question_text: Prevention strategies aiming at increasing the coping capacity of a population.
questions.explanation: Skill training and stress management are interventions to boost coping skills.

questions.question_text: Prevention strategies aiming at reducing the environmental risks associated with a disease.
questions.explanation: Changing environmental settings reduces risk exposures.

Taxation and legislative controls on tobacco and alcohol

questions.explanation: Advertising restrictions and public education aim to reduce demand.

questions.question_text: Harm reduction (Choose one option.)

options.text: Redesign the chemical structure of a psychoactive drug
Taxation and legislative controls on tobacco and alcohol

questions.explanation: Establishing a safe drinking limit is a harm-reduction approach.

questions.question_text: Supply or availability reduction (Choose four options.)

options.text: Redesign the chemical structure of a psychoactive drug
Taxation and legislative controls on tobacco and alcohol

correct_answers.text: Taxation and legislative controls on tobacco and alcohol

questions.explanation: Limiting availability involves controlling prescriptions, crop suppression, customs interdiction and taxing/regulating legal substances.
